messages:
sarah-support: Escalation: Customer (acct 987654321) can't reach our /v1/generate endpoint over PrivateLink. They report intermittent 502s and 403s, and DNS seems to resolve to the wrong account in some regions. Repro steps attached. Asking for help to triage — customer is on a shared VPC, we created a cross-account interface endpoint yesterday.

casebot: New escalation created: CASE-2026-1129. Priority: high. Assigning to #support oncall.

sarah-support: Quick repro we ran from customer's VPC:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'
*   Trying 10.10.10.45...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (10.10.10.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS handshake error: SSL: certificate subject CN=svc-prod-alb.amazonaws.com (expected api.redwood.example.com)
* Mark bundle as not supporting multiuse
* Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```
Also see intermittent 403s when hitting the same IP (auth error from proxy).

jake-sre: Thanks. Two quick asks: paste the output of `dig +short api.redwood.example.com` from the customer VPC resolver and `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=service-name,Values=*redwood* --query 'VpcEndpoints[*].[VpcEndpointId,VpcId,OwnerId,PrivateDnsEnabled]'` from our side. Also need the endpoint ENI IPs and the PHZ associations.

sarah-support: dig output from customer resolver: `10.10.10.45` (interface endpoint ENI IP). From their onprem resolver it's the public CNAME `svc-prod-alb.redwood-hosted.com` (public). Our describe output: `vpce-0a1b2c3d, vpc-0ff1, owner:111111111111, PrivateDnsEnabled: false`. Cross-account endpoint owner is 111111111111 (our infra account).

emily-netops: Interesting, PrivateDnsEnabled=false on the endpoint means the customer's hostnames won't automatically resolve to the endpoint DNS name. If they created a CNAME in their hosted zone pointing at our public ALB (svc-prod-alb.redwood-hosted.com), their resolver will sometimes hit the public ALB instead of the interface ENI depending on resolver rule order / split-horizon. That would explain TLS CN mismatch and intermittent 502 resets.

ryan-eng: Also saw this pattern before when teams create a cross-account VPC endpoint but forget to enable private DNS or create a PHZ association for the service name. For cross-account PrivateLink, two common safe configs: (1) enable Private DNS on the endpoint and rely on AWS to resolve the service name to vpce-*.amazonaws.com -> ENI IPs, or (2) create a Private Hosted Zone (api.redwood.example.com) and point CNAME -> vpce-<id>.<region>.vpce.amazonaws.com and associate the PHZ to the VPCs. Mixing public CNAMEs with an interface endpoint can route to the public ALB.

jake-sre: If customer is using STS assume-role for auth, hitting the public ALB could also cause our edge to drop tokens due to different host header or missing TLS SNI. Confirm whether requests that 403 include the same Authorization header as ones that succeed. Sarah, do you have raw request/response headers (sanitized)?

sarah-support: Provided sanitized headers from customer (attached to case): successful call header Host: api.redwood.example.com, Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, path /v1/generate. Failed call header Host: svc-prod-alb.redwood-hosted.com, Authorization present, but backend returned 403 with body {"error":"invalid_audience"}.

emily-netops: That "invalid_audience" smells like the token's audience is bound to api.redwood.example.com. When Host header is svc-prod-alb... our auth layer rejects it. So TLS cert CN mismatch -> curl shows cert for svc-prod-alb, and token audience mismatch -> 403.

ryan-eng: Action plan:
- Confirm if PrivateDnsEnabled can be turned on for the customer's vpce (if the endpoint was created cross-account with Private DNS disabled we might need to create a new endpoint or update it).
- If they prefer PHZ: create a private hosted zone for api.redwood.example.com in the customer's account pointing the A record to the interface endpoint DNS name (vpce-<id>.<region>.vpce.amazonaws.com) and associate the PHZ with the VPCs.
- Verify resolver rule priority: if they have an outbound resolver rule that resolves api.redwood.example.com to public CNAME, it will win. We need the conditional forwarder/PHZ ordering corrected.

jake-sre: Quick checks we performed that you can include in case notes:
```
# check endpoint owner/private-dns
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-id vpc-0ff1 --query 'VpcEndpoints[*].{Id:VpcEndpointId,Owner:OwnerId,PrivateDns:PrivateDnsEnabled}'

# list endpoint enis
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=description,Values=*vpce-0a1b2c3d*" --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].[NetworkInterfaceId,PrivateIpAddress,Status]'

# dig from customer resolver
dig @10.0.2.3 +short api.redwood.example.com
```

emily-netops: Also confirm there is no proxy or LB in the middle that rewrites Host header. Some customers have egress proxies that terminate TLS and re-initiate to remote with different SNI — that can surface as either cert mismatch or auth audience mismatch.

sarah-support: Customer confirmed they have an internal forwarder that resolves api.redwood.example.com -> public CNAME via central DNS (legacy). They can either update the forwarder to return the vpce ENI IP or we can assist with PHZ creation. Customer asked which option is recommended for long-term.

ryan-eng: Recommend PHZ associated to their VPC or enable Private DNS on the endpoint (if cross-account allowed). PHZ is more explicit and works well with split-horizon setups. Private DNS requires the endpoint owner to enable and is simplest for customers that don't want to manage PHZ.

jake-sre: Next steps for support thread:
- Sarah: tell customer to stop pointing CNAME -> public ALB. Instead, create A record in PHZ pointing to vpce ENI name or enable Private DNS.
- Emily: I'll prepare a short runbook for cross-account PrivateLink + PHZ association + sample Route 53 record we can paste in the case.
- Ryan: I'll check our infra account to see if we can enable Private DNS for vpce-0a1b2c3d (need owner consent).

deploy-bot: Note: Change attempt to enable PrivateDns on vpce-0a1b2c3d failed at 2026-11-29T15:09Z due to cross-account restriction. Manual PHZ route recommended.

sarah-support: I'll send the PHZ steps and a short checklist to the customer now and mark the case with the proposed resolution. Will follow up after they test. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jake-sre: Thanks — please ping here after they test. If they still see resets we should capture a pcap from within the VPC and the endpoint ENI for deeper trace.

sarah-support: Will do. Case updated: CASE-2026-1129 — awaiting customer PHZ changes.
